Create small demonstration calibration projects

Source: R/calibrar-auxiliar.R
calibrar_demo.Rd

Create self-contained example projects that can be used to learn the calibrar workflow, test installation, or prototype calibration code. Each demo writes a small set of files to disk and returns the information needed to read the setup table, load the observed data, define the model interface, and run a calibration.

Usage

calibrar_demo(path = NULL, model = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'calibrar.demo'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

path

Directory where the demo project should be created. If NULL, the current working directory is used.

model

Name of the demo model to generate. Supported values currently include "PoissonMixedModel", "PredatorPrey", "SIR", and "IBMLotkaVolterra".

...

Further arguments passed to print().

x

A calibrar.demo object returned by calibrar_demo().

Value

An object of class calibrar.demo, which also inherits from calibrar.results(). The returned list contains the demo project path, the true parameter values used to generate the synthetic data, the path to the calibration setup file, suggested starting values and bounds, phase information, model-specific constants, and a precomputed objective value at the true parameter set.

Details

The generated project is meant to be a compact, runnable example of the calibrar workflow rather than a realistic scientific application. The returned object typically contains enough information to proceed through the standard helper functions:

  • calibration_setup() to read the setup table,

  • calibration_data() to load the observed data,

  • calibration_objFn() to build the objective function, and

  • calibrate() or optim2() to run the optimisation.

The exact files created depend on model, but they usually include a calibration settings table, one or more observation files, and any required forcing or master data files.

The currently available demos are:

"PoissonMixedModel"

A Poisson autoregressive mixed model for the dynamics of a population observed at several sites over time.

"PredatorPrey"

A deterministic Lotka–Volterra predator–prey system solved numerically.

"SIR"

A simple susceptible–infected–recovered epidemic model solved numerically.

"IBMLotkaVolterra"

A stochastic individual-based predator–prey example.

See also

calibration_setup(), calibration_data(), calibration_objFn(), calibrate(), summary.calibrar.results(), print.calibrar.results()

Examples

tmp = tempdir()
demo = calibrar_demo(path = tmp, model = "PoissonMixedModel", T = 8, L = 3)
#> Creating observed data list for calibration...
#> Loaded observed data for variables: 'site_1', 'site_2', 'site_3'.
print(demo)
#> Calibration demo using model 'PoissonMixedModel'.
